messages:
jamie_ops: FYI getting a flood of reports — Dedicated allocations in na-east are failing with placement throttles (429) and some upstream 503s. Customers see increased latency and a billing mismatch alert for a few orgs. opening triage.
sara_support: customer ash_customer reported: 'calls to dedicated endpoint return 503 intermittently, then billing shows burst charge without traffic spike'. gave request id req-9a2b3c
michael_sre: looking at placement logs now. seeing repeated 'NoAvailableGPU' + 'PlacementThrottled' from placer v2.3 between 2456789100-2456789400. autoscaler seems to be oscillating: rapid scale-ups then immediate throttles.
lee_prodeng: could be the new quota enforcement change rolling yesterday. any trace of quota-deny in allocator? michael_sre can you paste sample logs
michael_sre: snippet:
```text
[2456789187] placer: allocate(pod=dedicated-pool-na-east, gpu_req=2) -> PlacementThrottled: backoff=120s
[2456789191] autoscaler: scale_up(pool=dedicated-pool-na-east) -> started
[2456789194] allocator: quota_check(org=ash-corp) -> OK
[2456789200] placer: allocate(...) -> NoAvailableGPU
```
ash_customer: seeing same — outage window ~ 2456789150-2456789300. We also got a billing alert from billing-bot saying 'unexpected surge detected' then it retracted. Not seeing traffic spike on our end.
billing-bot: Alert: anomaly_detected(org=ash-corp) severity=medium — token usage vs reported requests mismatch. investigate metering ingestion.
sara_support: requesting repro steps from customer: can you share a curl and timestamp? ash_customer sent curl with request id above. they were hitting /v1/dedicated/generate with model=redwood-xl and stream=false
michael_sre: hypothesis: allocator is decoupled from metering; if placer is throttling, fallback tries cross-region failover to us-west1 which triggers additional auth/billing path and causes duplicate metering pulses -> billing sees spike. also noisy tenant in na-east (tenant id tn-421) is spiking ephemeral allocations and causing oversubscribe.
lee_prodeng: confirm noisy neighbor? metrics show one tenant doing heavy batch inference: rn-tn-421 had 4x normal concurrent sessions starting 2456789000. can we throttle that tenant temporarily as mitigation?
michael_sre: we can apply per-tenant cap via routing policy: `route_override(tenant=tn-421, max_concurrency=2)` — applying now.
deploy-bot: route_override applied to pool dedicated-pool-na-east for tenant tn-421 by michael_sre at 2456789260
jamie_ops: mitigation step noted. Next: reduce placer aggressive backoff so placer retries faster to avoid cross-region failover thrash? current backoff config is exponential up to 120s.
lee_prodeng: propose reducing max backoff to 30s and add jitter. pushing a config change to staging now. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/placer/pull/482
sara_support: customer ash_customer — can you verify if errors stopped after ~2456789265? any continuing 503s?
ash_customer: errors dropped significantly after that time. still seeing one or two 503s around 2456789380 but overall service mostly healthy. thanks for quick action.
michael_sre: rolling change to backoff in prod with safety window 10m, will monitor. also found allocator metric: `failed_allocations_due_to_hot_pool` up by 150%.
jamie_ops: action items: (1) michael_sre keep monitoring for 30m, (2) lee_prodeng follow up PR to add soft-quotas for noisy tenants, (3) sara_support coordinate with ash_customer on post-mortem and billing reconciliation, (4) billing team to check metering duplicate pulses. tagging @billing-bot
billing-bot: Received task: investigate metering ingestion for org ash-corp — starting correlation job job-774 at 2456789320
michael_sre: noted a secondary bug: when placer falls back to cross-region, auth layer sometimes re-registers a token leading to double-counted embeds in metering. opening issue #998. will link repro.
lee_prodeng: thanks — I'll schedule follow-up for quota-hardening next sprint. anyone see customer-impacting regressions elsewhere? not in other regions.
jamie_ops: OK closing on-call loop for now; will reopen if alerts recur. :thumbsup:
